title: Sales and Inventory Tenant Remediation Readiness
method: Direct inspection of the current Sales and Inventory controller, service, and schema source. These checks describe recognizable source patterns; they do not prove runtime exploitability or enforcement.

controls.recommendation: Add JwtAuthGuard (or project-standard auth guard), resolve active organization membership from authenticated user + explicit organization selector, and pass verified context to every service method.
Replace model.find() with a query constrained by verified organizationId; include pagination and stable sort.
Set organizationId and createdBy server-side from verified context; reject/ignore client-supplied ownership fields.
Replace findByIdAndUpdate(id, ...) with findOneAndUpdate({_id:id, organizationId:context.organizationId}, sanitizedDto, ...); never allow tenant reassignment.
Add required organizationId field and tenant-aware uniqueness for orderId (compound unique index on organizationId + orderId); plan legacy data backfill before enforcing required.
Prove tenant A sees/updates only A records, tenant B cannot read/update A IDs, missing/inactive membership is denied, and client organizationId cannot reassign ownership.

implementationGuardrails: Do not deploy a partial tenant migration to production.
Backfill and verify legacy records before requiring organizationId.
Use compound unique indexes where identifiers are tenant-local; resolve duplicates before index creation.
Do not trust organizationId supplied in DTOs, query strings, or arbitrary headers without verifying active membership.
Add cross-tenant integration tests before closing each control.
Review related child records, exports, reports, aggregates, and audit events for the same scope.
